The task is to simulate stress in a perforated rectangular plate under gravity and an applied torque using FEniCS legacy (dolfin) with a small-strain linear elasticity solver.
The domain is a 2D rectangle of width 1.0 m and height 0.5 m, modeled in plane stress with unit thickness.
A circular hole of radius 0.1 m is centered at (0.5, 0.25) and remains traction-free.
A semicircular notch of radius 0.02 m is cut into the midpoint of the right edge, centered at (1.0, 0.25), so the notch concave arc is part of the domain boundary.
The material is linear elastic with Young's modulus E = 70e9 Pa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.33, density ρ = 2700 kg/m³, and gravitational acceleration g = 9.81 m/s² acting as a body force (ρ·g downward).
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law with unit thickness for the stiffness tensor.
The left edge (x = 0) is fully fixed: u = 0.
The applied torque is M = 800 Nm, converted to a tangential traction t_θ = M / (2π·r) = 800 / (2π·0.02) ≈ 6366 N/m².
The traction is applied only on the notch arc of radius 0.02 m, in the local tangent direction e_θ = (−sin θ, cos θ) at each point, oriented counterclockwise (positive θ) about the arc center at (1.0, 0.25).
The remaining right edge and the hole boundary are traction-free.
Discretize with a vector-valued Lagrange displacement space (P1 or P2) on a mesh with 64 elements per edge of the plate.
Solve the resulting linear system with a direct linear solver (e.g., built-in LU or MUMPS).
Post-process the Cauchy in-plane stress field (σxx, σyy, σxy) from the plane-stress law.
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane stress components and analyze displacement and von Mises stress patterns under the combined gravity and rotational loading.
The simulation is linear, so the sign of the torque only mirrors the solution; magnitudes of displacement and von Mises stress are unaffected.
